argument:
The bear is right that the legal adjustment does not repair FCF or financing needs. It does, however, prevent using the full reported margin contraction as evidence of recurring advertising economics collapsing; strong revenue growth and separately identified expenses are still relevant to that distinction.

Planned financing creates dilution uncertainty rather than a precisely quantified completed loss. I concede neither improving MACD nor prospective monetization establishes present valuation protection. The bull thesis survives as a conditional business-growth case that needs owner-cash improvement and confirmed price repair; it is not a reason to ignore dilution or buy an unconfirmed bounce.
key_points: Cash and price confirmation still required
rebuttal_to_previous: Concede cash flow and financing remain unresolved; legal adjustment narrows recurring-earnings inference without claiming to solve those separate issues.
